title: It was never about the staff.
paragraphs: It was never about the staff.
It was about the man who finally let go.
But what if the problem isn’t your lack of power—
It’s what you refuse to surrender?
There’s a moment most people miss in the story of Moses.
“What is that in your hand?” — Exodus 4:2
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable—
But something you grip so tightly it’s starting to define you more than God does.
Your need to be in control.
Some of us aren’t lacking power…
We’re just unwilling to let go.
He tried to be a deliverer in his own strength—and it ended in murder and exile.
Forty years reduced from prince… to shepherd.
Because what God asks you to release often feels like the only thing you have left.
We build our identity around it.
But here’s the truth that hits hard:
What you won’t surrender… will never be transformed.
“So Moses took the staff of God in his hand.” — Exodus 4:20
It was no longer just Moses’ staff.
It became the staff of God.
Later, that same staff was lifted over the sea:
“Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the LORD drove the sea back…” — Exodus 14:21
The power didn’t come from Moses.
It didn’t come from the staff.
Some scholars interpret the staff as a visible symbol of delegated authority—proof that Moses was acting under God’s command, not his own strength.
But Scripture cuts through that illusion:
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
That means the very thing you’re relying on…
Might be the thing blocking God’s power in your life.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because Moses’ story points to a greater one.
And on that cross stood what looked like weakness.
“He humbled himself by becoming obedient to death—even death on a cross!” — Philippians 2:8
Because we didn’t just need inspiration.
Our sin wasn’t a small mistake.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
But here’s the part that breaks chains—
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
Jesus took what we refused to surrender—
And He carried it to the cross.
That God is asking you to lay down?
You don’t need to fix yourself.
You need to fall at the feet of Jesus.
Because the same God who turned a staff into a sign…
Can turn your surrender into a miracle.
